note: The dedicated feature-audit track was lost to a runtime failure before it could publish its report. This inventory was rebuilt from the code by the owner-side pass and cross-checked against audit/findings/leaks.json and authz.json. Every DONE item was implemented and type-checked in this pass; every OPEN item names the exact file and what is missing.

findings.title: Nine public write endpoints only logged the submission and returned a fabricated success
findings.evidence: console.info(...) followed by NextResponse.json({ ok: true, message: 'Check your inbox for a confirmation.' }) — nothing was written anywhere. The same pattern in contact, pricing/lead, enterprise/lead, feedback, support, customer-requests, damages and quotations.
findings.impact: A visitor got a convincing success message and the enquiry was gone. Five of the nine endpoints are public and unauthenticated, so this was the normal path for every marketing enquiry.
findings.fix: Each endpoint now persists to a real table and returns an honest 503 when the write fails. New tables in db/migrations/004-marketing-forms.sql; shared writer in lib/api/public-submissions.ts.
findings.fix_notes: newsletter -> newsletter_subscribers; contact/pricing lead/enterprise lead -> contact_submissions (kind column separates them); feedback and customer-requests -> customer_requests; support -> support_tickets. The helper rejects unknown columns, binds every value as a parameter, and never logs PII. Public endpoints are rate-limited by lib/api/rate-limit.ts.

findings.title: /api/damages returned one hard-coded damage record for every landlord
findings.evidence: const stub = [{ id: 'DMG-204', title: 'Cracked bathroom tile — shower floor', property: 'Karen House 1', ... }]; return NextResponse.json({ count: stub.length, damages: stub })
findings.impact: Every landlord saw the same fictional damage on their dashboard, and the POST handler logged the real record without saving it.
findings.fix: GET now reads the caller's own rows scoped by user_id; POST now verifies the property and tenant belong to the caller and inserts a real row.

findings.title: /api/quotations always returned an empty array and discarded every write
findings.evidence: void status; void propertyId; void limit; return NextResponse.json({ count: 0, quotations: [] })
findings.impact: The quote workflow answered 'Quote request sent. Contractors will respond within 48h.' while storing nothing.
findings.fix: GET filters and returns the caller's quotes; POST verifies the property, the maintenance record and every contractor contact belong to the caller, then inserts a real row.

findings.title: The /dashboard/quotations page was a static shell with an empty array
findings.evidence: const quotations: Array<{...}> = []  — a module-level constant, never fetched.
findings.impact: The page rendered 'No quotations yet' permanently, whatever the database contained.
findings.fix: The page now reads the quotations table with the property and contact joins, derives the three stat cards from the real rows, and converts the KES minor-unit amounts for display. The 'New quote request' button now links to the maintenance page where quotes are actually created.

findings.title: Two pages resolved to the same route — app/page.tsx and app/(marketing)/page.tsx both mapped to /
findings.evidence: Both files existed and both rendered a marketing home page (230 and 228 lines). A route group does not change the URL, so Next.js sees two pages resolving to /.
findings.impact: A build-time route conflict on the site's most important URL. The build either errored or silently picked one.
findings.fix: The duplicate was removed and the more complete page (app/page.tsx, which includes the marketing header and footer) was kept.

findings.title: The public /status page always reported every system as operational
findings.evidence: A hard-coded allOperational = true with no probe of any kind.
findings.impact: The status page was decorative. It would have kept saying 'All systems operational' while the database was down.
findings.fix: It now uses the shared lib/system-health.ts probe, the same one the dashboard settings screen and /api/system/ping use.

findings.title: The /dashboard/settings/system screen asserted 'Everything is up to date' without checking anything
findings.evidence: A static card set with no database access.
findings.impact: The screen a landlord opens to check the system is healthy was a lie in the same way the status page was.
findings.fix: It now calls checkSystemHealth() and renders the real app version, schema version, database engine, health state and latency.

findings.title: The public health probe leaked the raw database error message
findings.evidence: ...(health.db_error ? { db_error: health.db_error } : {}) on an unauthenticated endpoint.
findings.impact: A Postgres error can carry the database host, database name, schema and table names. This is exactly the infrastructure exposure the owner asked about, introduced by the health refactor.
findings.fix: The public response now carries only ok / db / latency_ms / schema_version / timestamp. The error detail stays in the server log and on the authenticated dashboard screen.

findings.title: Airtel Money is offered as a rent payment method with no Airtel integration anywhere
findings.evidence: The payment-method marketing copy lists Airtel Money; the only mobile-money integration in the codebase is Safaricom Daraja (M-Pesa).
findings.impact: A promise the product cannot keep. A tenant who picks Airtel Money cannot pay.
findings.fix: NEEDS-PRODUCT-DECISION: either remove Airtel Money from the payment-method copy, or build the integration. This is a copy-and-product call, not a code fix.

findings.title: Fabricated customer case studies with attributable quotes are publicly rendered and API-exposed
findings.evidence: Named customers with specific quotes and metrics, presented as real case studies.
findings.impact: Publishing invented customer quotes is a legal and reputational exposure, and the privacy page claims data you do not have.
findings.fix: NEEDS-PRODUCT-DECISION: replace with anonymised or clearly-labelled illustrative examples, or remove them. This needs the owner's call on what is true.

findings.title: The privacy policy and help centre promise an account-deletion control that does not exist
findings.evidence: The policy describes a data-deletion right; there is no DELETE /api/account route and no deletion path in lib/actions.ts.
findings.impact: A published legal promise the application cannot honour. The founder is the data controller here, so this is a real compliance gap, not a nit.
findings.fix: NEEDS-PRODUCT-DECISION, but the work is clear: add a DELETE /api/account route that removes the user's rows across every table (including c2b_transactions, which has no FK to tenants and therefore survives a tenant delete) and anonymises what must be retained for accounting.

findings.title: The dashboard reads sensitive tenant columns straight from the browser
findings.evidence: The page queries the tenants table from the client and selects national_id, phone and free-text notes.
findings.impact: Any column-level encryption has to move these reads behind the server first, otherwise the ciphertext is what arrives in the browser. This blocks the encryption rollout.
findings.fix: Blocked by CRYPTO-025. The encryption track's design doc section 11.1 calls this out as PHASE 0 — move the sensitive reads behind a server route before encrypt-on-write is switched on.

findings.title: Dead links in the public navigation — Discord invite, forum, office hours, press assets
findings.evidence: Links pointing at '#' or at pages that do not exist.
findings.impact: Broken links in the primary navigation of a site about to launch.
findings.fix: Remove the dead entries or point them at real destinations before launch.

findings.title: Fabricated download counts, vote counts, changelog releases and status-page incidents
findings.evidence: Hard-coded template download counts, roadmap vote counts, a changelog of releases that were never shipped and status-page incidents.
findings.impact: The marketing site makes factual claims that are not true. Low security impact, real credibility impact, and it is the kind of thing a first paying customer notices.
findings.fix: NEEDS-PRODUCT-DECISION: either zero the counters until real traffic exists, or source them from real data.

findings.title: The public security page promises an audit log and login rate limiting that did not exist
findings.evidence: The page makes security claims about audit logging and rate limiting that the codebase did not implement.
findings.impact: A published security page is a commitment. Either build the control or amend the page.
findings.fix: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by this pass: rate limiting now exists (lib/api/rate-limit.ts) on the public write endpoints, and an audit-log design is part of the hardening work. The page copy must still be reconciled with what is actually deployed.

findings.title: The public copy claims row-level security on every table and three data-residency regions
findings.evidence: The primary database is Neon Postgres with no row-level security — tenancy is enforced in application code — and there is no region pinning.
findings.impact: A false claim in a legal document about the security architecture of a platform holding national ID numbers.
findings.fix: Correct the copy to describe what the platform actually does, or implement what it claims. The application-level tenancy model is defensible; saying it is RLS is not.

findings.title: Sample documents are published as public binaries and are stale relative to their generator
findings.evidence: Pre-generated .docx files under public/ that no longer match lib/templates/templates.ts.
findings.impact: A user downloads a document that is not the document the product would produce today.
findings.fix: Regenerate them at build time (the prebuild-templates script already exists) and stop committing the binaries.

findings.title: Placeholder analytics claims and an unused analytics dependency
findings.evidence: @vercel/analytics is a dependency; the placeholder numbers are hard-coded.
findings.impact: Low. Wire up real analytics or remove the claim.
